title: Early district pianists
summary: Dawson names Alfred Wilson, Tony Jackson and Robert Caldwell, none of whom he worked with.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Do you remember any of the other pianists? We were just talking about Fest being one of the great pianists in the district, but you might have been around there even a few years earlier than Fest. Do you remember any other pianists?
The very first ones you remember that worked in the district? Let's see.

They had another father there, but it was a good pianist. Well, maybe I can remember. I can't think of his name. Talking about Alfred Wilson. Alfred Wilson. Tony Jackson. Tony Jackson was a good pianist. Did you ever work? No. Did you ever work? No. Yeah, yeah. I never worked with them fellas. Robert Caldwell.

He was a sissified. He had a brother named George Collar. He was a shoemaker. He was a clarinet player. Uptown. Well Bob Caldwell, the district went down. He got a job working and why you working? With the bank when he jumped out the window. It was Bob Caldwell.
